intro: Buying a home in Florida involves more than comparing property prices and mortgage interest rates. Homeowners insurance, hurricane coverage, property taxes and community association fees can significantly affect your monthly housing expenses.

Our free Florida mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly payment before purchasing a home. Whether you are considering a property in Miami, Orlando, Tampa, Jacksonville or another Florida community, enter your financing details and estimated ownership costs to establish a realistic budget.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Florida?

blocks.markdown:
A $360,000 Florida home purchased with a 20% down payment and a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,726.71.

The example assumes no private mortgage insurance. Taxes, insurance, association fees and interest rates are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

Florida offers a diverse housing market, including coastal condominiums, suburban single-family homes, retirement communities and inland properties.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Florida housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/FL/INC910224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $359,000 during the 2020–2024 survey period. Homeowners with mortgages reported median selected monthly ownership costs of $1,959.

These historical figures provide a useful starting point, but they cannot tell you the current purchase price of a particular property.

A waterfront home may involve considerably different insurance premiums and maintenance expenses from a similarly priced inland property. Condominiums can also have substantial monthly association fees.

When using the calculator, enter the expected purchase price of the specific property rather than relying exclusively on statewide housing statistics.

sections.heading: How to Use the Florida Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Begin with your anticipated home purchase price and the amount you have available for a down payment.

Enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender and select a repayment term. A 30-year mortgage generally offers lower monthly principal and interest payments than a 15-year mortgage with the same rate.

Next, enter your expected annual property taxes and insurance premiums.

If separate hurricane or flood insurance is required, include those premiums without counting any coverage twice. Add monthly HOA or condominium association fees where applicable.

Review your estimated total monthly housing payment and amortization schedule.

Try different purchase prices, down payments and interest rates to understand how each variable affects affordability. You can also use our national Mortgage Calculator to compare financing arrangements outside Florida.

sections.heading: How Florida Property Taxes Affect Mortgage Payments

blocks.markdown:
Florida property taxes depend on assessed property values, applicable exemptions and local millage rates.

County property appraisers establish property valuations, while local taxing authorities determine the rates used to calculate tax liabilities.

For example, assume a property's taxable value is $320,000 and its combined applicable millage rate is 15 mills.

Annual property tax would be:

$320,000 × 0.015 = $4,800

This equals $400 per month.

The example uses a hypothetical taxable value and millage rate. Your actual bill may include additional assessments or charges.

### Florida homestead exemption

Qualifying homeowners who use their Florida property as their permanent residence may receive a homestead exemption that reduces taxable property value.

Different portions of the exemption apply to different categories of taxes, and certain exemption amounts are subject to inflation adjustments.

Visit the [Florida Department of Revenue's property tax exemption guide](https://floridarevenue.com/property/pages/Taxpayers_Exemptions.aspx) and contact your county property appraiser to confirm eligibility and current exemption amounts.

Do not subtract an assumed exemption from every portion of your property tax calculation.

### Save Our Homes assessment limitation

Florida's Save Our Homes provision limits annual assessment increases for qualifying homestead properties.

The annual increase is generally capped at the lower of 3% or the relevant change in the Consumer Price Index, subject to applicable rules.

The [Florida Department of Revenue's assessment limitation guidance](https://floridarevenue.com/property/Pages/ConsumerPriceIndex.aspx) explains how this calculation works.

This limitation can create a significant difference between a property's market value and its existing assessed value.

### Property tax reassessment after purchasing a home

When ownership changes, a property's assessment generally resets to its just value, subject to applicable exceptions and portability provisions.

Consequently, the seller's existing property tax bill may substantially underestimate what you will pay.

Use the county property appraiser's new-homebuyer tax estimation resources wherever available.

Insurance deserves particular attention when purchasing a Florida home.

Premiums can depend on roof condition, construction materials, property location, replacement cost and exposure to severe weather.

Obtain insurance quotes before finalizing your purchase rather than waiting until your mortgage closing date.

### Hurricane insurance deductibles

Some Florida homeowners policies contain separate hurricane deductibles expressed as a percentage of dwelling coverage.

For example, a 2% hurricane deductible on a policy with $350,000 in dwelling coverage represents $7,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered loss.

A lower insurance premium may therefore come with a substantially higher financial risk.

The [Florida Department of Financial Services' hurricane deductible guide](https://www.myfloridacfo.com/division/consumers/consumerprotections/floridashurricanedeductible) explains how these deductibles operate.

### Flood insurance

Ordinary homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding. Some mortgage lenders require separate flood coverage depending on the property's location and applicable lending rules.

Check the property's flood designation using the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Even properties outside designated high-risk flood areas can experience flooding.

Add the annual cost of applicable flood insurance to your mortgage calculator inputs.

sections.heading: HOA, Condominium and Community Development District Fees

blocks.markdown:
Florida buyers should investigate charges associated with planned residential communities and condominium developments.

Association fees may support shared facilities, landscaping, building maintenance, security and insurance.

Review the association's budget, reserve funding and any proposed special assessments before purchasing a property.

Some developments also belong to Community Development Districts, commonly called CDDs. District assessments can help finance infrastructure and public services.

These charges may appear on the property tax bill. Avoid counting them again as separate monthly expenses if they are already included in your annual tax estimate.

Condominium buyers should also investigate building inspection requirements and future repair obligations, which can affect association budgets and ownership costs.

The Florida Housing Finance Corporation offers financing and assistance programs through approved participating lenders.

### Florida Housing Homebuyer Program

The [Florida Housing Homebuyer Program](https://floridahousing.org/programs/homebuyer-overview-page) provides eligible applicants with 30-year fixed-rate mortgage options.

Applicants generally need to meet credit score, household income, purchase price and homebuyer education requirements.

County-specific limits apply, so consult a participating lender before selecting a property.

### Florida Assist

Florida Assist provides eligible buyers with up to $10,000 toward qualifying purchase expenses.

The assistance is structured as a zero-interest deferred second mortgage rather than an unconditional grant.

Repayment may become due when the property is sold, refinanced or no longer occupied as the borrower's primary residence, among other qualifying events.

Compare the complete financing arrangement before accepting assistance.

### Other mortgage assistance options

Florida Housing also offers additional assistance arrangements associated with qualifying first mortgages.

Program funding and eligibility requirements can change. Do not include assistance in your budget until an approved lender confirms that you qualify and funds are available.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Florida?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract regular household expenses.

Florida does not impose an individual state income tax, but homeowners still face federal taxes, payroll deductions, insurance expenses and property-related charges.

Use our [Florida Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/florida-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate existing debt obligations.

Allow room for potential insurance premium increases, maintenance costs and hurricane-related deductibles.

When comparing mortgage offers, review the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's homebuying resources](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/) to understand borrowing costs and lender disclosures.

A lender's approval amount should not automatically become your household's maximum purchase budget.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $360,000 Florida home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year loan term, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,726.71. Property taxes, insurance and association fees increase your total housing expenses.

### Does buying a Florida home change its property tax assessment?

Generally, yes. An ownership change can reset the property's assessed value, meaning the previous owner's tax bill may not reflect your future liability. Contact your county property appraiser for an updated estimate.

### Should flood insurance be included in a Florida mortgage calculator?

Yes, if you expect to purchase flood coverage. Include its annual premium alongside other applicable insurance costs. Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding, and certain mortgage arrangements require separate coverage.

Use our Florida mortgage calculator to compare financing options and property-related expenses before making an offer.

Obtain property-specific tax estimates, insurance quotes and association information whenever possible. Understanding these costs early can help prevent unexpected financial pressure after purchasing your Florida home.
